profiles.description: Community-corroborated read-only BMS map for the Mk1 (pre-facelift) MG ZS EV. Every installed command and formula is confirmed by an independent implementation (OVMS vehicle_mgev) against the pinned primary CSV.
limitations: The primary source vehicle is one Australian 2021 MG ZS EV; the 2019-2021 Mk1 span and market invariance come from the independent OVMS vehicle_mgev implementation, which serves UK/EU and TH/AU Mk1 vehicles with this exact DID map.
Mk1 only: the facelifted 2022+ ZS EV moves its BMS to 7E5/7ED and is not covered by this profile. A 2022-registered pre-facelift Mk1 is outside the confirmed year range and cannot be selected.
Range DID B0CE was removed from the installable set: OVMS polls it but leaves its decode disabled, so no independent source confirms the scale.

Battery-Emulator decodes the MG5 (not ZS EV) temperature DIDs with a different offset; the installed half-degree formulas follow the two ZS-EV-specific sources. Treat temperature values with care until physically validated.
Telltale has not physically validated this mapping on an MG vehicle; expected responder 789 remains an ISO 15765 physical-address inference.

Temperature ranges are copied from the pinned source CSV, whose lower bounds are 0 degC; a physically legitimate sub-zero battery or coolant reading therefore fails closed as out-of-range instead of displaying.

Signal-level exclusions from the 2026-09 cross-source review: resistance DID B045 (its unit and magnitude are backed by the primary source alone, and 0-8190 ohm is not physical for a pack) and the B058/B059 cell-index bytes (no second source attests them). The cell min/max voltage readings themselves remain corroborated and shipped.

profiles.description: Searchable REEV research entry for BMW i3 REx 60 Ah.
limitations: The generation metadata covers i3 variants but does not establish a safe REx-specific battery command set.
Research index only; no command from this entry is installed by Telltale.

Actively excluded from executable tiers (2026-09 review): every SME battery poll requires ISO 15765-2 extended addressing — target address 0x07 as the first data byte of request 0x6F1, tester address 0xF1 leading every 0x607 response frame, and a flow-control frame that itself carries the 0x07 prefix. Three independent pinned implementations agree (OVMS vehicle_bmwi3 @ 587a91d7, dala Battery-Emulator @ 8e63222e, WiCAN i3 profile @ bc3ae6d4 — the last marked PRO-hardware-only), and none shows an 11-bit standard ISO-TP alternative. Telltale’s ELM327 stack has no ATCEA/ATFCSM support, so these commands cannot be sent correctly. The DID layer itself (0xDDBC SoC, 0xDD68 pack V, 0xDD69 pack A, 0xDDC0 temps, 0x6335 SoH) is cross-corroborated and recorded for a future stack that gains extended addressing.

profiles.display_name: Lexus RX450hL 2020 Premium source vehicle probe
profiles.description: One-shot read-only experimental subset backed by a pinned 2020 RX450hL source-vehicle profile and published sample artifact.
limitations: The pinned project evidence is one 2020 Lexus RX450hL Premium source vehicle; market, ECU firmware, and applicability to any other trim are not established.

The pinned profile directly declares 7E2 to 7EA, Mode 21 PIDs 61/62/63/95, formulas and ranges. Public artifacts support the byte slices, while the full exact payload length is a conservative Telltale contract rather than independently published raw-frame proof.
RX450h, RX450hL model years 2021-2022, and the unresolved PID 98 pack-voltage decoding are explicitly excluded from this experimental probe.

Telltale permits only a user-triggered one-shot read after per-connection consent. It never scans identifiers, changes diagnostic session, unlocks security, writes, controls, retries automatically, installs these values, or mixes them into the dashboard.
Telltale has not physically validated this mapping on a Lexus vehicle.

Cross-source review (2026-09) found no independent confirmation of the claimed signal byte windows: the Ircama ELM327-emulator Toyota hybrid scenario documents 2161/2162 as MG temperatures at payload byte 0 and 2195 as internal resistance, and no consulted source attests the torque/voltage windows this profile decodes. The profile therefore stays experimental.

profiles.description: Community-corroborated read-only E-GMP BMS map, confirmed across OVMS, WiCAN and OBDb and against pinned real response captures.
limitations: Cross-source community mapping: every installed formula agrees byte-for-byte across independent implementations (OVMS, WiCAN, OBDb) and decodes pinned real-vehicle response captures to physically plausible values. Telltale has not physically validated it on this vehicle.

Exact-length contract: the profile accepts only a 59-byte 220101 and 43-byte 220105 payload from responder 7EC. A firmware answering with a different shape fails closed - a dark gauge, never a guessed number.
Responses are multi-frame ISO 15765-2; an adapter or clone that mishandles flow control will time out rather than corrupt values.
Pack current is signed: positive while discharging, negative while charging or regenerating.
Bit-packed status flags (charging, relay, ignition) and cumulative operating time are not imported; the formula engine installs numeric gauges only.
Pack voltage bounds are derived from cell-count physics (2.8 V x 144s to 4.2 V x 192s) so both the 58 kWh and 77.4 kWh packs stay in range; an out-of-range reading is refused, not shown.
Battery inlet temperature is excluded on E-GMP: OVMS and OBDb disagree on its decode (signed vs offset-40), and a disagreement means exclusion.

profiles.description: Community-corroborated read-only BMS map for the 32.3 kWh (usable) gen2 e-up!: SoC agreed by OVMS and WiCAN, pack voltage by OVMS and iternio, each replayed against pinned e-Golf same-BMS captures.
limitations: Per-signal source matrix: SoC 028C is agreed by OVMS vehicle_vweup and the WiCAN e-up profile (iternio dissents, recorded); pack voltage 1E3B is agreed by OVMS and iternio (WiCAN corroborates the DID via its MEB profile only). No single pair covers both installed signals; each signal names its own two counted sources. Telltale has not physically validated this vehicle.

payload_length evidence is sourcePartial: exact 1-byte (028C) and 2-byte (1E3B) payloads are proven by real captures of the same DIDs on the e-Golf's same-supplier BMS and by ISO-TP single-frame math, not by an e-Up capture. The exact-length contract fails closed on any other shape.

SoC here is the BMS absolute SoC (raw/2.5; the byte scale's ceiling is 255/2.5 = ~102, an encoding bound, not a reachable reading): expect it to differ from the instrument-cluster display by a few percent — the one pinned real-car point (wican-fw discussion #190) shows 95.6 published at a dash-indicated 100%. The display SoC (DID 1DD0 on 765->7CF, raw/2) is known from OVMS only and is therefore not installed.

Pack current (1E3D) is excluded: OVMS decodes (raw-2044)/4 while iternio's eUP file says (raw-2048)/10 — a slope and zero-point conflict with no second e-Up source to break the tie. (e-Golf captures prove 2044//4 on that model's BMS, but that is cross-model evidence.)
iternio's eUP file scales 028C as /2.55; OVMS and WiCAN agree on /2.5 (and iternio's own MEB file uses /2.5 as its base). The 2-of-3 agreement is installed; the dissent is recorded.
Pack voltage bounds derive from cell-count physics sourced from OVMS code (gen2 = 84 cells in series): 2.8 V x 84 = 235.2 to 4.2 V x 84 = 352.8. An out-of-range reading is refused, not shown.
Vehicle production ended in 2023; year_to is public knowledge, not source-pinned (sources say '2020 onwards').

Market scope: the gen2 e-up! was sold in Europe only; the two fleet-serving implementations (OVMS vehicle_vweup, the WiCAN e-up profile) serve European fleets — iternio, counted only for the 1E3B scale, is a global service and neither supports nor weakens the market scope, matching the platform-scoped market treatment of the E-GMP community entries.

Independence audit for the SoC pair: the WiCAN e-up profile entered wican-fw in original commit af008049d18276ea15e418f660892a3a125aa730 (2024-09-02) with no OVMS attribution and a different representation (PCI-offset B4 convention against OVMS FromUint8), and wican-fw discussion #190 shows an e-up! owner's real-car 22028C response decoding through this profile (WiCAN reported SOC 93.2 and the maintainer and owner both confirmed the profile works), with issue #235 as later same-platform usage. A shared ancestry in community wiki knowledge cannot be positively excluded and is recorded here; the MG ZS EV community entry rests on the same OVMS-and-WiCAN pairing precedent.

profiles.description: Community-corroborated read-only EVC battery map for Renault Zoe phase 1 (Q210/Q90/R240/R90/R110), cross-confirmed between CanZE and WiCAN with OVMS and ABRP as supporting sources.
limitations: Cross-source community mapping: every installed formula agrees byte-for-byte between CanZE (operative ZOE/_Fields.csv) and WiCAN (Renault Zoe R110.json); Telltale has not physically validated it on this vehicle.

All installed commands are single-frame UDS Mode 22 reads from the EVC (7E4 -> 7EC, 11-bit): no diagnostic session, no flow-control override, no extended addressing is required. CanZE polls these same DIDs with per-ECU 'Session required = 0' and WiCAN polls them with a plain ATSP6 init.

Pack voltage is NOT installed, for independence, not disagreement: DID 223203 (LBC voltage, (A*256+B)*0.5) has CanZE as its only independent source — the OVMS Zoe mapping embeds CanZE's CSV verbatim and therefore cannot count as a second source — and the alternative DID 222004 is corroborated only by a WiCAN window whose byte indexing would fold the DID echo into the value (a constant >=512 V on a 400 V pack). One clean source is not two; the profile ships SOC, pack current, SOH and battery rack temperature only.

SOC DID 222002 is the BMS/'real' HV-battery SOC (CanZE equates it to free-frame 0x42e SOC). The dashboard 'user SOC' is not exposed through any Mode 22 DID in any source; expect readings a few percent different from the instrument cluster.
Pack current sign: offset-binary (raw-32768)*0.25; positive while discharging per OVMS StandardMetrics usage.

payload_length values are inferred (sourcePartial): max field extent per DID in Renault-DDT-derived CanZE ZOE/EVC_Fields.csv plus WiCAN reading exactly those bytes; no pinned raw response capture was available.

The battery temperature DID 222001 exists on two ECUs: on EVC 7E4->7EC it is battery rack temperature (A-40); on BCB 792->793 the same DID number is mains phase current. The command pins request header 7E4 and responder 7EC, so the collision is inert.
The DID map is EVC firmware (phase 1) specific; Zoe Ph2 / ZE50 uses a completely different, 29-bit-only DID set (see the Ph2 candidate) and must never inherit this profile.
Market scope: nearly the entire Ph1 fleet and both counted implementations (CanZE, WiCAN) are European; the treatment mirrors the platform-scoped market handling of the other community entries.

Year-range evidence: the 2012-2019 span is not a public-knowledge guess — the pinned CanZE application code routes every Ph1 variant (Q210, R240, Q90, R90/R110) to the single ZOE/ field table these commands are built from, while Ph2/ZE50 gets a separate table, so the installed contract is pinned to the whole Ph1 generation.

limitations: Cross-source community mapping: every installed formula agrees byte-for-byte across independent implementations (SoulEVSpy, WiCAN) on the byte-identical Kona OS layout. Telltale has not physically validated it on this vehicle.

Exact-length contract: the profile accepts only a 59-byte 220101 and 43-byte 220105 payload from responder 7EC. No SK3-specific raw capture existed at the pinned revisions; the exact payload lengths inherit from the byte-identical Kona OS layout (as the Niro EV profile does), corroborated by WiCAN's 9/7-frame pid suffixes and SoulEVSpy's parser requiring consecutive frames 21-28 / 21-26.
Responses are multi-frame ISO 15765-2; an adapter or clone that mishandles flow control will time out rather than corrupt values.

Pack current is signed: positive while discharging, negative while charging or regenerating. SoulEVSpy decodes it as explicit two's complement, independently confirming the OS-family sign convention; WiCAN decodes with an inverted sign for this family (documented quirk), so the installed convention follows SoulEVSpy signedness at the family byte positions.
The SK3 e-Soul was not sold in North America; the profile is global for the markets that received it (Korea, Europe and others).
Bit-packed status flags (charging, relay, ignition) and cumulative operating time are not imported; the formula engine installs numeric gauges only.

Year scope is narrowed to 2020, the single model year the primary source (SoulEVSpy) attests on a real e-Soul; WiCAN records no year. SK3 production spans 2019-2023 and the BMS contract is expected to match across it, but that extension is uncorroborated, so later years stay outside the installable identity until attested.

Battery temperatures (max, min, inlet) are excluded: both model-explicit sources decode them with an unsigned simplification, so the signed semantics every sub-zero reading depends on has no second e-Soul source. Positions agree across sources; the semantics do not clear the community bar, and a winter number shown on family convention alone is exactly the plausible-wrong-number this catalog exists to refuse.
